item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption reported on the consequences of losing its ability to refer cases directly to the Director of Public Prosecutions.
item.support: If the Commission is to refer a matter for prosecution, it must now refer the matter to South Australia Police (SAPOL).

item.text: The report compared the referral process before and after the legislative changes and considered arrangements in other jurisdictions.
item.section: The ICAC Act post 7 October 2021; Other jurisdictions
item.support: As I stated earlier, all other anti-corruption bodies around Australia can refer matters to the Director in their jurisdiction.

item.text: The Commissioner concluded that the restrictions reduced independence, duplicated work, caused delay and obstructed direct contact with prosecutors.
item.support: The loss of the Commission’s independence, double handling, delay and the lack of direct communication with the prosecutor

item.text: The single recommendation sought a legislative amendment restoring direct referrals to the Director of Public Prosecutions.
item.support: The ICAC Act be amended to reinstate the capacity for the Commission to refer a matter

item.quote: The loss of the Commission’s independence, double handling, delay and the lack of direct communication with the prosecutor are all consequences of the current position.
